questions.text:
class A { private n = 1 }
console.log(new A().n)

class A { protected n = 4 }
console.log(new A().n)

class A { #n = 1 }
console.log("n" in new A())

abstract class A { n() { return 1 } }
console.log(new A().n())

namespace N { export const n = 1 }
console.log(N.n)

const o = { n: 1 } as const
;(o as { n: number }).n = 2
console.log(o.n)

function isNum(x: unknown): x is number { return true }
const x = "ab"
console.log(isNum(x))
console.log(x.length)

function id<T>(x: T): T { return x }
console.log(id(3))

function f(this: { n: number }, x: number) { return this.n + x }
console.log(f.length)

class A { n!: number }
console.log(new A().n)

enum E { A = 1, B = "b" }
console.log(E.B)

enum E { A, B }
console.log(Object.keys(E).length)

enum E { A = "a", B = "b" }
console.log(Object.keys(E).length)

enum E { A = 1, B = 2, C = 4 }
console.log(E.A | E.B)

class A { private constructor() {} }
console.log(typeof new A())

function f(...xs: [number, number]) { return xs[0] + xs[1] }
console.log(f(2, 3))

const o: { [key: string]: number } = { a: 1 }
console.log(o.b)

enum E { A = 1, B = A * 2 }
console.log(E.B)

console.log(0 || 5)
console.log(0 ?? 5)
Why can code outside the class read a private field after compilation?
options: private is erased, so the field stays an ordinary property
private becomes a WeakMap that throws
private renames the field to a symbol

questions.text: What is a # field at runtime?
options: An ECMAScript private name that another class body cannot read
A new WeakMap on every read

questions.text: What does abstract on a class become in the emitted JS?
options: A flag that makes new throw
Nothing. The constructor stays an ordinary function

questions.text: What is a namespace after emit?
options: A class with a private constructor
An object that holds the exported values

questions.text: What does as const change at runtime?
options: Nothing. The value stays an ordinary mutable value

questions.text: What does satisfies change at runtime?
options: Nothing. The expression is checked and emitted unchanged
It wraps the value in a Satisfies object

questions.text: What does a type predicate x is T mean for the returned boolean?
options: A true result converts the value to T
In the true branch the checker treats the value as T. The boolean itself is ordinary
It writes a hidden brand onto the object

questions.text: What is the this parameter?
options: A way to make function.length equal 2
A check on the call's this. It is erased from the parameter list

questions.text: What does the mark n!: number on a class field do?
options: It leaves the field uninitialized and only silences the checker

questions.text: Which enum members get a reverse mapping?
What merges when a class and a namespace share a name?
options: Nothing. The namespace replaces the class
One value: the constructor plus the namespace exports

Where does an asserts function's throw come from?
options: From the throw written in the body. The asserts keyword is erased

questions.text: How many constructors does a class with constructor overloads emit?
options: Two: a public one and a private one

questions.text: What does an index signature [key: string]: number create at runtime?
options: Nothing. It only types reads and writes

questions.text: What does a constraint T extends string do?
options: It converts the argument to string at the call
It creates a separate function for string
It stops the generic function from running
It is checked when the type argument is chosen and is not a runtime check
